name: Diocletian's Edict on Maximum Prices 301 AD
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The earliest documented major price-control failure, and a case study Austrians return to for 1,700 years. T1: in 301 AD, after decades of debasing the silver denarius to pay his armies, the Roman emperor DIOCLETIAN issued an Edict on Maximum Prices covering over 1,000 goods and services -- from wheat and wine to a barber's shave and a scribe's day-wage -- with the penalty for violation set at DEATH. T2: he blamed the merchants for the price rises he himself had caused by minting more coins with less silver; the edict's own preamble curses the 'unbridled fury' and 'greed' of sellers. T3: the seen-and-unseen result: within weeks, goods DISAPPEARED from the open market (SEEN: no wheat in the stalls); merchants preferred to hoard, to sell only to family, or to move goods to black markets in other cities (UNSEEN: the merchant who normally traded openly is now hiding, and the buyer who could have bought openly is now paying more, in secret, in a smaller supply). T4: Lactantius, a contemporary Christian writer, records in his 'On the Deaths of the Persecutors' that MUCH BLOOD WAS SHED for the sake of small and cheap things, and that as goods vanished the edict was quietly ABANDONED within about a decade. T5: modern Austrian economists (Rothbard's 'Egalitarianism as a Revolt Against Nature' and Sowell's 'Basic Economics') treat Diocletian's Edict as the founding case study of price-controls-under-inflation: the emperor debases the coinage, prices rise as sellers demand more of the weaker coin, the emperor blames the sellers rather than his own mint, the ceiling is imposed, the goods disappear, and the ceiling is eventually withdrawn. Further rungs: fragments of the edict survive on stone in over 100 places across the eastern empire (Aphrodisias in Turkey has the fullest copy); Diocletian abdicated in 305, the only Roman emperor to voluntarily step down; his palace at Split, Croatia, still stands.
source: PRIMARY: fragments of the Edict on Maximum Prices (Latin: Edictum de Pretiis Rerum Venalium), especially the Aphrodisias copy; Lactantius, De Mortibus Persecutorum ch. 7. CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Edict on Maximum Prices' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- 301 AD date, over 1,000 items, death penalty, Lactantius's 'much blood was shed' account, the edict's silent abandonment within a decade, its survival on stone in over 100 inscription-sites, Aphrodisias as the fullest surviving copy. Rothbard, Egalitarianism as a Revolt Against Nature (essay collection) and Man Economy and State ch. on price controls; Sowell, Basic Economics ch. 3 'The Role of Prices'. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: the exact Lactantius wording; whether the edict's coverage is best stated as 'over 1,000 goods and services' vs a narrower list.
framing_note: SCENE-LED case-study ladder that anchors the ENTIRE price-controls tradition to a specific emperor and a specific year. Dinner-test payoff: T1 (death penalty for selling wheat above the ceiling) and T3 (the goods simply DISAPPEARED within weeks -- the merchant would rather hoard than sell at a loss). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: this is a SEEN-VS-UNSEEN ladder -- SEEN is the low mandated price on the tablet; UNSEEN is the wheat that never appears in the market, the merchant who moves his stall to a black market, the family that goes hungry because the shelf is empty. ACCURACY RAILS: the 1,000+ figure is defensible; do NOT invent specific prices unless quoting the Aphrodisias inscription; Lactantius is a partisan (anti-Diocletian Christian) source, cite him by name. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: stem describes the debased coinage, the edict, and the death penalty; the answer is the RESULT (goods disappeared / merchants hoarded / black markets formed) or the REASONING MOVE (the seller's incentive to withdraw supply when forced to sell below cost). DISTRACTOR MINE: other reasoning moves used honestly against other cases (knowledge problem for USSR planning, moral hazard for bailouts, Cantillon effect for money-printing); other historical emperors' economic acts (Justinian's Corpus Juris Civilis, Constantine's solidus, Nero's coin debasement). CHOICE PARITY: if the answer is 'the goods disappeared from the shelves', distractors are other real market-response patterns (prices rose openly, quality collapsed, queues formed) applied to other real cases.
history_overlap: HISTORY owns Diocletian as an emperor and the Tetrarchy as a political arrangement; economics owns the price-control mechanism and Lactantius's testimony on its economic effects.

name: Emperor Julian's grain-price ceiling in Antioch 362 AD
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The case Thomas Sowell returns to again and again as proof that the price-control reasoning-error is not a modern mistake. T1: in the winter of 362 AD, the emperor JULIAN (the last non-Christian Roman emperor, called 'the Apostate') was wintering in ANTIOCH preparing his Persian campaign; the city was suffering food shortages after a bad harvest and rising grain prices. T2: Julian ORDERED the grain price capped at a low level and imported his own imperial grain to sell at that price. T3: the seen-and-unseen result played out immediately -- Antioch's merchants and surrounding-region farmers WITHDREW their grain from the market rather than sell at a loss; the imperial grain was quickly bought up (often by the same merchants for resale on the black market), and the shelves went empty again. T4: Julian, furious, wrote a public pamphlet -- the MISOPOGON ('Beard-Hater') -- blaming the Antiochenes and their merchants for greed and 'godlessness', never blaming the ceiling itself. Julian died a few months later on the Persian campaign in June 363; the ceiling was quietly ended. T5: Thomas Sowell in Basic Economics uses Julian's Antioch as proof that the price-control reasoning-error is IDENTICAL across 1,700 years: a ruler orders a price low, the goods vanish, the ruler blames the sellers rather than the arithmetic. Sowell's teaching move -- 'compared to what?' -- applies: any critique of high grain prices in Antioch must name the counterfactual (higher prices with grain on the shelves vs low prices with empty shelves). Further rungs: Julian's pamphlet Misopogon survives complete and is one of the very few first-person books written by a Roman emperor; Antioch is modern Antakya in southern Turkey.
source: PRIMARY: Julian, Misopogon (composed at Antioch, winter 362-63); Ammianus Marcellinus, Res Gestae Books 22-23. CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Julian (emperor)' and 'Misopogon' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- Julian's Antioch winter, the grain-price intervention, the imperial-granary imports, the shortages, Julian's public pamphlet blaming Antiochenes for their greed and irreligion, his departure and death on the Persian campaign June 363. Sowell, Basic Economics 5th ed., ch. 3 'The Role of Prices' -- Julian's Antioch used explicitly as the recurring case study of the eternal price-control reasoning-error. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: Sowell's exact phrasing about Julian in the current edition of Basic Economics; the specific tone of the Misopogon's complaint about the merchants.
framing_note: A twin case-study to Diocletian -- same reasoning-error, different emperor, 61 years later, and a rare case where the ruler himself wrote a public complaint about the result. Dinner-test payoff: T4 (the emperor wrote an ENTIRE ANGRY PAMPHLET blaming the merchants for the shortage HE HAD CAUSED). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: SEEN-VS-UNSEEN with a bonus 'blame-the-messenger' rung -- Julian sees the empty shelves and blames the seller's character rather than his own ceiling. ACCURACY RAIL: Julian is NOT 'Julian the Apostate' in the stem's first line (that is a Christian polemical name assigned later); the bank's neutral history-voice calls him 'the emperor Julian' or 'the last non-Christian Roman emperor'. SYMMETRIC-VOICE: told with the same neutral analytic voice one would give any recurring reasoning-error case. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: describe the winter shortage, the ceiling, the disappearing grain, and let the answer be Sowell's move ('compared to what?'), or the pamphlet, or the specific market response (farmers withheld supply). DISTRACTOR MINE: other 'ruler blames merchants for shortage his own policy caused' cases (Mugabe 2007 Zimbabwe, Maduro 2013 Venezuela); other price-control tools used honestly (rationing, imports, quotas).
history_overlap: HISTORY owns Julian as a late-Roman political figure and his Persian campaign; economics owns the reasoning-move that his Antioch ceiling exemplifies.

name: 1973 oil shock and US gasoline price controls
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The 1970s gasoline lines were caused by the price controls, not by the embargo. T1: on OCTOBER 17, 1973, in response to US arms shipments to Israel during the Yom Kippur War, the Arab members of OPEC declared an OIL EMBARGO on the United States and other Israel-supporting countries; world oil prices roughly quadrupled over a few months. T2: the US already had Nixon-era gasoline PRICE CEILINGS in force. Rather than let the pump price rise to clear the market, the government kept prices capped and imposed rationing rules including ODD-EVEN-LICENSE-PLATE purchase days (you could only buy on odd-numbered dates if your plate ended in an odd digit). T3: the visible result was GASOLINE LINES that stretched for hours at every filling station; some stations posted 'NO GAS' signs and closed for the day. Meanwhile in West Germany and Switzerland -- which had NO price controls -- gas prices rose sharply and there were NO LINES. T4: Murray ROTHBARD's 1974 essay 'The Energy Fiasco' laid out the seen-vs-unseen chain: the SEEN was the low pump price on the sign; the UNSEEN was the value of the two hours of a person's life spent in line, the deliveries not made, the trips not taken, and the imported gasoline that private importers were unwilling to bring in at a loss. Milton Friedman said the same thing on his Newsweek columns and later 'Free to Choose'. T5: the reasoning move: a shortage under a price ceiling is a shortage IN SPACE (empty pumps) AND IN TIME (hours of queueing) -- the ceiling has not eliminated the cost, it has converted the money-cost into a TIME-COST that everyone pays but no producer collects. When the ceilings were unwound by 1981 under Reagan, gasoline lines vanished within months even though prices remained high. Further rungs: the embargo formally ended March 1974, but US price controls on domestic 'old oil' persisted until January 28, 1981; California in 1979 during the Iranian Revolution oil-price shock ALSO had lines because its state price controls remained.
source: PRIMARY: Rothbard, 'The Energy Crisis: A Libertarian View' (Reason magazine, 1974) and 'The Case Against the Fed' (1994); Milton Friedman, Free to Choose (1980), ch. on 'The Anatomy of Crisis'. CONSULTED: Grokipedia '1973 oil crisis' and 'Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- October 17 1973 embargo date, the price controls already in force from Nixon 1971, odd-even-license-plate rationing, the West-Germany-vs-US natural experiment, the January 28 1981 Reagan decontrol executive order, the immediate disappearance of the lines after decontrol. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact wording of Rothbard's 'Energy Fiasco' phrase (title may be 'The Energy Crisis: A Libertarian View'); Reagan's decontrol EO number.
framing_note: The textbook seen-vs-unseen case study for a whole generation, and one of the natural experiments Austrian economists cite most often because West Germany's price-free response gives a clean counterfactual. Dinner-test payoff: T3 (in West Germany there were no lines) and T5 (the time-cost in line is the cost the price didn't visibly show). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: SEEN-VS-UNSEEN with the T5 refinement that a price ceiling converts money-costs into TIME-costs -- it does not eliminate the cost. ACCURACY RAIL: the embargo was OCTOBER 17 1973 (not August, not September); price controls preceded the embargo by two years, which is the load-bearing point. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: stem describes the embargo, the ceilings, the odd-even rationing, and the West-German counterfactual; the answer is the REASONING MOVE (time-cost substitution, seen-vs-unseen) or the SPECIFIC POLICY EVENT (Reagan's 1981 decontrol EO). DISTRACTOR MINE: other 1970s energy events (1979 Iranian Revolution oil shock, Carter's 1977 National Energy Plan, Alaska Pipeline 1977 completion), other ceiling-to-time-cost cases (rent control's queue-and-connections allocation, wartime rationing).
history_overlap: HISTORY owns the Yom Kippur War and OPEC as a political-diplomatic entity; economics owns the domestic-price-ceiling mechanism and its documented queue-shortage effects.

name: Carter's Windfall Profits Tax on oil 1980
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The 1980 tax that pretended to be about fairness but functioned as a price control. T1: in APRIL 1980, President Jimmy CARTER signed the Crude Oil Windfall Profit Tax Act, imposing an excise tax on the difference between the market price of domestic crude oil and a lower government-set 'base price'. T2: the pitch to the public: oil companies were making 'windfall' profits from the 1979 Iranian Revolution oil-price shock, and the tax would recover those for the public good. T3: the seen-and-unseen result: because the tax raised the effective cost of producing each additional barrel of US oil, domestic production FELL rather than rose in response to high prices -- the Congressional Research Service later estimated a REDUCTION of US oil output of somewhere between 3% and 6% and INCREASED oil imports by similar amounts through the 1980s. T4: the reasoning move: a windfall-profits tax is functionally a PRICE CEILING on producer revenue -- Bastiat's 'unseen' would say the barrels of domestic oil that were never drilled, the wells never sunk, the workers never hired in Texas or Oklahoma, are all costs that never appear in the news the way 'oil-company profits' do. Ronald REAGAN campaigned against the tax; it was formally repealed in 1988 as prices declined and the tax collected almost nothing. T5: the modern echo: whenever a 'windfall tax' on any industry is proposed (banks 2008, oil again 2022, drug companies 2020), the same reasoning-move applies -- kid learns to ask 'what will the taxed producers do LESS of, and who bears that cost invisibly?' The lesson is not that windfalls are moral; it is that the market has already priced in the risk of shortages, and taxing the reward removes the incentive to produce during the crisis when society most needs it. Further rungs: the Congressional Research Service 1990 report is the standard cited source for the reduced-output estimate.
source: PRIMARY: Crude Oil Windfall Profit Tax Act of 1980; Congressional Research Service report 'The Crude Oil Windfall Profit Tax of the 1980s' (Salvatore Lazzari, 2006). CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Crude Oil Windfall Profit Tax Act of 1980' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- April 1980 signature, base-price mechanism, 1988 repeal, CRS-cited reduction of domestic output 3-6% and corresponding import increase. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact CRS report title and year; whether the 3-6% figure is best cited as CRS 1990 or CRS 2006.
framing_note: A case study that teaches kids to recognize a tax-shaped price control. Dinner-test payoff: T3 (the tax made US oil production DROP -- exactly the opposite of what a country supposedly worried about 'energy independence' would want) and T4 (the barrels never drilled are Bastiat's unseen). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: SEEN-VS-UNSEEN (visible: fair-sounding tax on 'windfall' profits; unseen: barrels that never come out of the ground) + INCENTIVE RECOGNITION (a tax at the margin reduces production at the margin). ACCURACY RAIL: the 3-6% figure is a range for a reason; do not overclaim; the CRS report is the source. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: stem sets up the 1979 shock, the 1980 tax, the fairness framing; the answer is the REASONING MOVE (Bastiat's unseen: undrilled barrels) or the SPECIFIC OUTCOME (US production fell, imports rose). DISTRACTOR MINE: other tax-shaped price-control cases (2022 UK energy windfall tax, 2008 bank bailout tax proposals, drug-price-negotiation proposals framed as taxes on excess profit).
history_overlap: HISTORY owns Carter's presidency broadly; economics owns the incentive analysis of the tax.

name: New York City's rent control since 1943
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The great American case study of a 'temporary' wartime price control that became permanent for 80+ years and destroyed the housing stock. T1: in NOVEMBER 1943, at the height of World War II, the federal Office of Price Administration froze RENTS in New York City as a wartime emergency measure. T2: after the war the federal freeze was handed off to New York STATE, then to New York City itself; a series of laws (the Emergency Housing Rent Control Law 1946, the Rent Stabilization Law 1969, the Emergency Tenant Protection Act 1974) kept SOME form of rent regulation continuously in force from 1943 to the present -- the 'temporary' program is now over 80 years old. T3: the seen-and-unseen: SEEN was the low rent stamped on the lease of a lucky tenant; UNSEEN were the apartments that were never built, the landlords who let buildings decay because rent below cost meant no maintenance was worth it, the vacant units KEPT OFF the market to avoid getting a rent-controlled tenant, and the ARSON epidemic of the 1970s in the South Bronx that Assar Lindbeck himself connected to the incentive to burn a rent-controlled building for the insurance. T4: the Swedish economist Assar LINDBECK, a democratic-socialist and Nobel-committee-adjacent figure and not a right-winger by any stretch, wrote in The Political Economy of the New Left (1971): 'In many cases rent control appears to be the most efficient technique presently known to destroy a city -- except for bombing.' Rent-control critics from across the ideological spectrum cite this line more than any other. T5: the modern natural experiment came in 2019 when New York STRENGTHENED rent regulation with the Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act; within two years the number of rent-regulated apartments held OFF the market ('warehoused' by landlords) rose sharply, and construction of new rental housing in NYC dropped, exactly as the seen-vs-unseen analysis predicted. Further rungs: Milton Friedman + George Stigler's 1946 pamphlet 'Roofs or Ceilings?' is the first classic rent-control critique; Chris Palmer + Rebecca Diamond's 2019 American Economic Review study of San Francisco rent control found similar housing-stock destruction.
source: PRIMARY: Assar Lindbeck, The Political Economy of the New Left (1971) -- the 'except for bombing' passage; Milton Friedman + George Stigler, 'Roofs or Ceilings? The Current Housing Problem' (Foundation for Economic Education, 1946); Rebecca Diamond, Tim McQuade + Franklin Qian, 'The Effects of Rent Control Expansion on Tenants, Landlords, and Inequality: Evidence from San Francisco' (American Economic Review 2019). CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Rent control in New York' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- 1943 federal freeze, subsequent state and city laws, the 1969 stabilization law, the 2019 HSTPA, the warehousing phenomenon, the South Bronx arson pattern. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: Lindbeck's exact wording (some sources render it 'best way to destroy'); the specific date of the 1943 federal order; the 2019 HSTPA's specific provisions.
framing_note: The flagship rent-control case study, chosen because it runs 80+ years and thus has a decisive empirical track record. Dinner-test payoff: T4 (a Swedish democratic-socialist economist compared rent control to BOMBING as a way to destroy a city). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: SEEN-VS-UNSEEN (visible tenant benefit vs invisible housing-stock destruction) + INCENTIVE RECOGNITION (landlord's incentive to warehouse or under-maintain a rent-controlled unit). ACCURACY RAIL: Lindbeck's quote is famous; verify the exact wording; do not attribute it to Friedman or Sowell (both quote it but Lindbeck said it). Second rail: this ladder must not descend into anti-tenant framing -- the answer names the mechanism that hurts FUTURE tenants (fewer units, worse maintenance), not present ones. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: stem sets up the 1943 freeze, the 80-year continuity, the specific decay pattern; the answer is Lindbeck's move, or the empirical mechanism (warehousing, arson, under-maintenance), or the classical critique (Friedman-Stigler 1946). DISTRACTOR MINE: other 20th-century rent-control cities (SF, Berkeley, DC, Berlin, Stockholm, Buenos Aires); other seen-vs-unseen housing cases (zoning, minimum-lot-sizes, parking mandates).
history_overlap: HISTORY owns NYC's WWII home-front administration broadly; economics owns the rent-control mechanism and its 80-year housing-market consequences.

name: San Francisco rent control: Diamond, McQuade, Qian 2019
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The most-cited modern empirical study of what rent control does to the housing stock of a city. T1: San Francisco imposed RENT CONTROL on buildings built before 1980 under a 1979 ordinance; then in 1994 a ballot measure (Proposition I) extended rent control to small multi-family properties (2-4 units). T2: Stanford economists Rebecca DIAMOND, Tim MCQUADE, and Franklin QIAN used the 1994 expansion as a NATURAL EXPERIMENT -- comparing small multi-family properties that just crossed into rent control against otherwise-identical properties that just missed the cutoff. The study appeared in the American Economic Review in September 2019. T3: the finding for existing tenants was that yes, they saved on rent -- so the SEEN benefit was real. But the UNSEEN was that landlords of the newly-controlled properties reduced the supply of rental housing by 15% relative to the counterfactual -- some converted units to condominiums, some demolished and rebuilt as unregulated new construction, some undertook renovations that removed units from the rental market. T4: the reasoning-chain payoff: the study concluded that the housing-supply reduction PUSHED UP city-wide rents by about 5% -- meaning rent control TRANSFERRED wealth from FUTURE tenants (who face higher rents in a smaller market) to CURRENT protected tenants (who save on the specific unit they occupy). Diamond herself, in interviews, framed the result as a WEALTH TRANSFER, not a housing solution. T5: Sowell's move: 'compared to what?' Rent control in SF vs. a policy of easing zoning to permit more housing construction produces radically different empirical trajectories -- and the study is not ideology, it is a natural experiment in a single city. The Austrian point is not 'markets are perfect', it is that ANY intervention has SEEN and UNSEEN consequences, and this study measured both. Further rungs: Diamond is not an Austrian; she is a mainstream Stanford economist; her result is empirically identical to what Friedman + Stigler predicted in 1946.
source: PRIMARY: Rebecca Diamond, Tim McQuade + Franklin Qian, 'The Effects of Rent Control Expansion on Tenants, Landlords, and Inequality: Evidence from San Francisco' (American Economic Review, September 2019, vol. 109 no. 9). CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Rent control in San Francisco' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- 1979 ordinance, 1994 Proposition I expansion, the Diamond-McQuade-Qian identification strategy, the 15% supply reduction, the 5% city-wide rent increase, the wealth-transfer framing. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact figures in the published AER version; the specific year of Proposition I.
framing_note: A REASONING-move ladder that uses one specific modern empirical study as its case. Dinner-test payoff: T4 (rent control INCREASED city-wide rents by 5% -- helping current tenants at future tenants' expense). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: SEEN-VS-UNSEEN as an empirically-measured effect; SOWELL 'COMPARED TO WHAT?' as the T5 move. ACCURACY RAIL: the AER paper's numbers are precise -- 15% supply reduction, 5% city-wide rent rise -- verify at build. Do not overclaim; the study is one city and one policy expansion. Second rail: the authors are not Austrians; presenting them as such would misrepresent the evidence base. The point IS that a mainstream empirical study confirmed Friedman-Stigler 1946. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: stem sets up the 1994 SF expansion, the natural-experiment design, the supply reduction; the answer is the CITY-WIDE RENT EFFECT (rents rose) or the REASONING MOVE (wealth transfer to current tenants at future tenants' expense). DISTRACTOR MINE: other rent-control empirical studies (Berlin 2020, Berkeley 1980s Chris Palmer studies, Stockholm queue length), other natural-experiment studies in housing policy (LIHTC crowd-out, Section 8 studies).
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns San Francisco as a place; economics owns the rent-control mechanism and the empirical study of its effects there.

name: Stockholm's twenty-year apartment queue
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The world's longest housing queue and what it teaches. T1: Sweden imposed nationwide rent control during WWII (1942), extended it as permanent policy after the war, and centralized rental allocation in Stockholm through a public housing queue called BOSTADSFORMEDLINGEN ('the Housing Bureau'). T2: because rents are set below the market-clearing level by negotiation between tenant unions and landlord associations (a system called BRUKSVARDESHYRA), the demand for a rental apartment in central Stockholm massively exceeds supply, and units are allocated by TIME IN THE QUEUE rather than by price. T3: as of the early 2020s, the average waiting time for a first-hand rental contract in central Stockholm was approximately 20 YEARS; the longest documented waits exceed 30. Parents SIGN THEIR CHILDREN UP TO THE QUEUE AT BIRTH so the child has a shot at a first-hand rental contract by age 20. T4: Assar LINDBECK, again -- writing about his own country -- named rent control as the reason for the queue, and Swedish center-right and even some center-left economists agree; the reform-blocker is not economics but the political power of the tenants' union (Hyresgastforeningen), a textbook Olson dispersed-cost / concentrated-benefit case. T5: the seen-and-unseen play out at generational scale: SEEN is the young couple in a nice central-Stockholm apartment paying a below-market rent; UNSEEN are the twenty years the couple next door queued in shared housing, the second-hand rental black market that emerged (often illegal sublets at 3-5x the controlled rent), and the young families who simply left Stockholm rather than wait a generation for housing. The reasoning move: when a price does not clear the market, SOMETHING ELSE must -- and that something is queueing, connections, black markets, and exit. Further rungs: the second-hand-sublet black market is documented by Stockholm's own police reports and by the housing think-tank Timbro.
source: PRIMARY: Bostadsformedlingen Stockholm annual reports (queue-length statistics); Lindbeck, The Political Economy of the New Left (1971) with his 1990s revisions; Andreas Bergh + Magnus Henrekson, 'Government Size and Growth' (Journal of Economic Surveys, 2011) with housing sub-analysis; Timbro (Swedish free-market think-tank) housing reports. CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Rent regulation in Sweden' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- 1942 wartime origin, bruksvardeshyra system, Bostadsformedlingen queue, ~20-year average wait in central Stockholm, sign-your-child-up practice, black-market sublet phenomenon. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact current queue length (the 20-year figure is the widely-cited Bostadsformedlingen average); Lindbeck's specific writing on Swedish rent control.
framing_note: The generational-scale rent-control ladder that shows the mechanism at its most extreme. Dinner-test payoff: T3 (Swedish parents sign their children up TO THE HOUSING QUEUE AT BIRTH) -- a fact that stops a dinner-table conversation cold. REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: SEEN-VS-UNSEEN (protected tenants vs 20-year queue) + WHEN-PRICE-DOESN'T-CLEAR-SOMETHING-ELSE-MUST (queueing, connections, black market, exit) as the T5 move. ACCURACY RAIL: 20 years is the widely-cited AVERAGE in central Stockholm; peripheral Stockholm is shorter (5-10). Second rail: this is not a Swedish-bashing ladder -- Sweden has world-class free-market policies in other domains (school vouchers, low corporate tax); rent control is a specific policy exception. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: stem describes the queue-based allocation, the sign-child-at-birth practice, the illegal sublet market; the answer is the REASONING MOVE (non-price allocation must use SOMETHING) or the SPECIFIC MECHANISM (queueing, black market). DISTRACTOR MINE: other non-price-allocation cases (Soviet bread lines, US 1973 gas queues, wartime rationing, US public housing waiting lists).
history_overlap: GEOGRAPHY owns Stockholm as a city; economics owns the queue-and-sublet consequences of the Swedish rent-control system.

name: Berlin's 2020 rent freeze (Mietendeckel)
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The natural experiment Germany ran on itself in 15 months. T1: on FEBRUARY 23, 2020, the Berlin state government (a red-red-green SPD/Linke/Green coalition) enacted the MIETENDECKEL ('rent lid'), a five-year freeze on rents in ~1.5 million Berlin apartments and a mandatory rent-CUT for units above certain per-square-meter thresholds. T2: the rule was Berlin-specific -- neighboring German cities and the rest of Germany kept market pricing -- creating a clean natural experiment. T3: within months of enactment, the supply of rental apartments listed on the market in Berlin DROPPED by roughly 50% while listings in adjoining non-Berlin municipalities ROSE; the ifo Institute in Munich and the DIW Berlin both documented the shift. Landlords held units off the market, listed as unfurnished furnished shares (exempt), or converted to sale. T4: rents on the SHRINKING pool of remaining Berlin listings actually ROSE for new lettings (because supply had collapsed while demand had not), so the policy simultaneously benefited tenants who already had a lease and PUNISHED tenants trying to move. T5: on APRIL 15, 2021 the German Constitutional Court (Bundesverfassungsgericht) struck the Mietendeckel down on federalism grounds -- rent regulation is a federal competence, and Berlin lacked the authority. Retroactive rent had to be paid back. The Mietendeckel ran 15 months; the ifo + DIW empirical evidence is now the standard modern European case study of rent-control-shock supply response. Further rungs: the Berlin S-Bahn saw a documented uptick in COMMUTERS coming in from Brandenburg during the Mietendeckel period, one visible sign of tenants pushed out to non-controlled suburbs.
source: PRIMARY: Gesetz zur Neuregelung gesetzlicher Vorschriften zur Mietenbegrenzung (Berlin law, Feb 23 2020); Bundesverfassungsgericht ruling 2 BvF 1/20 (April 15 2021); ifo Institute studies by Andreas Peichl et al. (2020-21); DIW Berlin studies by Konstantin Kholodilin et al. (2020-22). CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Mietendeckel' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- February 23 2020 enactment, five-year design, mandatory rent-cut thresholds, the ~50% supply reduction on new listings, the April 15 2021 constitutional strike-down, retroactive back-payment. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact ifo and DIW figures for supply reduction; the Bundesverfassungsgericht decision number.
framing_note: A modern EUROPEAN rent-control ladder deliberately chosen because it happened in 2020-21 in a rich Western democracy with excellent economic statistics. Dinner-test payoff: T3 (rental supply on the market fell about 50% within months) and T4 (the shrinking supply meant NEW-tenant rents actually ROSE, so the policy hurt exactly the movers it was supposed to help). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: SEEN-VS-UNSEEN with the specific supply-collapse mechanism + INCENTIVE RECOGNITION (landlord's rational response to forced-below-cost pricing is to withdraw from the market). ACCURACY RAIL: the constitutional strike-down was on FEDERALISM grounds, not price-control-is-unconstitutional grounds -- the Court did not rule the policy bad, only that Berlin was the wrong level of government to enact it. name: Argentina's 2020 rent-control law and its 2023 repeal
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The three-year natural experiment Milei made a campaign issue. T1: in JUNE 2020, under the Peronist government of Alberto Fernandez, Argentina passed Ley 27.551, a rent-control law that mandated three-year minimum leases, annual rent adjustments only by a specific index (BCRA formula tied to wages + inflation), and other tenant protections. T2: within a year, the seen-and-unseen: SEEN was the protected tenant on the three-year lease at an indexed rent. UNSEEN was the rental supply -- Buenos Aires realtors' associations reported new-listing supply falling by roughly 40-50% in the first year and rents on the remaining listings rising SHARPLY (tripling or more in nominal terms by 2023, even accounting for Argentina's already-high inflation). T3: landlords responded rationally: many withdrew units from long-term rental into short-term (Airbnb, unfurnished-monthly), some converted to sale, some kept units EMPTY rather than commit to a three-year contract at an indexed rent under Argentina's political inflation risk. T4: Javier MILEI, an economist and self-described anarcho-capitalist / Austrian-school follower, campaigned in 2023 on repealing Ley 27.551 among many other reforms; he won the presidency in November 2023. On DECEMBER 29 2023, one of his first Decreto de Necesidad y Urgencia (DNU 70/2023) actions was to REPEAL the rent-control law. T5: within months of repeal, new-listing supply in Buenos Aires ROSE roughly 3x, and rents on NEW listings fell in real terms as competition returned. The natural experiment ran from June 2020 to December 2023, then the reverse-experiment ran through 2024 -- and both matched the seen-vs-unseen prediction to a striking degree. The reasoning move: an intervention that reduces the profitability of supplying rental housing will reduce the quantity supplied. Further rungs: Milei's DNU 70/2023 was constitutionally challenged; the rent-decontrol part survived; the fuller results are being tracked by CEMA and other Buenos Aires economics institutes.

name: Venezuela's Fair Price Law and the empty shelves 2013-2016
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The most recent large-scale price-control catastrophe, in a rich oil-country, in the lifetimes of today's ten-year-olds. T1: Hugo CHAVEZ died March 5, 2013, having won the October 2012 election; Nicolas MADURO succeeded him after a narrow April 2013 election. Venezuela was already living under Chavez-era price controls on food, medicine, and consumer basics; Maduro extended them. T2: in JANUARY 2014, Maduro passed the LEY ORGANICA DE PRECIOS JUSTOS (Fair Price Law), setting maximum retail prices on hundreds of items, jailing merchants for 'unjust' pricing, and creating a new agency (SUNDDE) to enforce it. T3: the seen-and-unseen played out in weeks: SEEN were the low mandated prices posted on the shelves of Mercal and PDVAL (state supermarkets); UNSEEN were the shelves themselves -- FLOUR, COOKING OIL, MILK, RICE, TOILET PAPER, SOAP disappeared, and Venezuelans began queueing for hours (sometimes overnight) at any store rumored to have received a shipment. Toilet paper became a political news story in 2013. T4: the black market ('bachaqueo') took over most consumer commerce; the government responded with FINGERPRINT-INDEXED rationing (Sistema Biometrico) and eventually the CLAP boxes -- state-distributed food packages linked to political loyalty, distributed only through neighborhood collectives (Comites Locales de Abastecimiento y Produccion) with proven allegiance to the government. T5: the reasoning-move chain: price controls -> supply withdrawal -> queues -> rationing -> political-loyalty allocation. When market prices are abolished, SOMETHING ELSE allocates goods -- and that something becomes political power. Every socialist calculation-debate prediction (Mises 1920) reappeared inside three years in a rich, oil-producing, previously-middle-income country. Further rungs: hyperinflation followed (CPI peaked around 130,000% in 2018 per IMF estimates); by 2024, ~7.7 million Venezuelans had left the country -- the largest displacement crisis in modern Western Hemisphere history.

CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Economic policy of the Nicolas Maduro government' and 'Shortages in Venezuela' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- Fair Price Law 2014, empty-shelf pattern, fingerprint rationing, CLAP boxes, ~7.7M emigrants by 2024, IMF ~130,000% CPI peak 2018. REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: SEEN-VS-UNSEEN + KNOWLEDGE-PROBLEM + the political-loyalty-allocation move that shows what fills the vacuum when prices don't. ACCURACY RAIL: Venezuela's collapse is a MULTI-cause event (oil-price collapse 2014, sanctions from 2017, monetary chaos); the PRICE-CONTROL slice is one causal channel among several -- do NOT overclaim price controls as the sole cause; DO establish that the empty-shelf phenomenon began before major sanctions and tracked the Fair Price Law's enforcement. name: Venezuela's Bitcoin mining and the CLAP-box economy
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: Two things that filled the vacuum left by price controls, on opposite sides of the same country. T1: because Venezuelan electricity was heavily subsidized (a form of price control -- the price of electricity capped far below production cost) and the bolivar hyperinflated, Venezuelans discovered they could MINE BITCOIN with essentially-free electricity and hold sound money instead of the collapsing bolivar. By 2018, Venezuela had one of the largest per-capita Bitcoin-mining populations in Latin America. T2: the government responded not with a market-reform but with a POLICE campaign -- SEBIN (the political intelligence service) and later SUPCACVEN raided mining operations, seizing rigs, and by 2023 the government banned mining outright, citing 'electricity grid stability'. T3: on the other side of the same economy, the CLAP boxes (Comites Locales de Abastecimiento y Produccion) -- state-distributed food parcels -- became the sole reliable food source for millions of Venezuelans, distributed ONLY through neighborhood collectives that could verify political loyalty (typically membership in the ruling PSUV party, showing up at pro-government rallies, voting where instructed). T4: journalist Anatoly Kurmanaev and researcher Anibal Sanchez documented the CLAP-loyalty pattern in a series of reports for the New York Times and Reuters 2016-2019; testimony from Venezuelan opposition figures like Maria Corina Machado and Leopoldo Lopez corroborates that CLAP allocation was political. T5: the reasoning-move payoff: this is the single clearest modern natural experiment showing that when GOVERNMENT-SET prices replace MARKET prices, allocation MUST fall back on some other mechanism -- and in Venezuela the two mechanisms that emerged were (a) the underground global market via Bitcoin (for those with technical skill and rig access) and (b) political loyalty via CLAP (for everyone else). Mises 1920's prediction that a fully price-controlled economy 'gropes in the dark' was answered by Venezuela's actual response: political intimidation for the poor, and a global crypto-network for the technical. Further rungs: Alejandro Machado + Jill Carlson's 2019 Human Rights Foundation report on Bitcoin in Venezuela is the standard cited source.

CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'CLAP (Venezuela)' and 'Cryptocurrency in Venezuela' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- CLAP as state-distributed food parcels with documented loyalty-conditional distribution, Bitcoin mining as electricity-arbitrage under subsidized power, SEBIN raids on miners, 2023 outright mining ban. REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: KNOWLEDGE-PROBLEM RECOGNITION (Mises's prediction that a price-abolished economy falls back on non-price allocation) + the specific 'political power fills the vacuum' consequence. ACCURACY RAIL: the CLAP loyalty-conditional finding is well-documented but must be attributed to specific journalists / researchers, not asserted as bare fact. name: Cuba's Special Period 1990-1994
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The natural experiment Cuba ran when its Soviet subsidy vanished. T1: from 1959 to 1990 the Cuban economy was cushioned by billions of dollars per year in Soviet subsidies -- fuel at below-world-market prices, guaranteed sugar-purchase quotas at above-world prices, industrial inputs. When the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, that subsidy vanished essentially overnight; the years 1990-1994 in Cuba are called the PERIODO ESPECIAL EN TIEMPO DE PAZ ('Special Period in Time of Peace'). T2: Cuba's price controls, rationing (LIBRETA), and central-planning apparatus stayed in place -- Cuba did not liberalize prices. The result: the average Cuban lost between 5 and 25 pounds of body weight during 1990-1993, per multiple public-health studies; caloric intake dropped from ~3,100 kcal/day in 1989 to ~1,900 kcal/day in 1993. T3: the pet-population collapse: with meat scarce, the URBAN CAT AND DOG populations of Havana collapsed; ethnographers and journalists documented that some pets were eaten and many others starved or were abandoned. Zoo animals were similarly affected. T4: what Cuba DID allow was small-plot urban agriculture -- ORGANOPONICOS in Havana and other cities -- and legalization of self-employment in certain trades (1993 dollarization decree also opened limited private commerce). These MARKET concessions (not the price controls) are what began the slow recovery; when Cubans could grow and sell food, they did. T5: the reasoning-move payoff: Cuba's Special Period is the natural experiment that isolates SOCIALIST CENTRAL PLANNING from the confounding variables of war, sanctions, or bad harvest -- the subsidy simply vanished, the planning apparatus remained, and the empirical result was an average-weight collapse of a whole population. The recovery came through market openings (organoponicos, dollarization, tourism). This is Mises 1920's prediction demonstrated at the level of a nation's body weight. Further rungs: Ben Corbett's This Is Cuba (2002) is one accessible chronicle; Fidel Castro himself gave 1993 speeches acknowledging the caloric collapse (blaming the US embargo).
source: PRIMARY: Manuel Franco et al., 'Impact of energy intake, physical activity, and population-wide weight loss on cardiovascular disease and diabetes mortality in Cuba, 1980-2005' (American Journal of Epidemiology 2007); Ben Corbett, This Is Cuba (2002); ONE (Cuba's Oficina Nacional de Estadisticas) historical data. CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Special Period' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- 1990-1994 duration, Soviet subsidy loss, caloric drop from ~3100 to ~1900 kcal/day, 5-25 pound average weight loss, urban pet population collapse, organoponicos, 1993 dollarization and self-employment decrees. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact caloric figures (Franco et al. 2007 is the peer-reviewed anchor); the 5-25 pound weight-loss range.
framing_note: A rare NATURAL EXPERIMENT that isolates central planning from other confounds -- the subsidy vanished, everything else stayed, and the empirical result was catastrophic. Dinner-test payoff: T2 (the average Cuban LOST 5-25 pounds because the food-planning system could not adapt) and T3 (urban PETS were eaten). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: KNOWLEDGE-PROBLEM (planning cannot adapt to a shock) + the market-opens-help move (organoponicos + self-employment being what began recovery). ACCURACY RAIL: this is a Cuban tragedy, not a bash-Cuba ladder -- caloric and weight figures come from PEER-REVIEWED public-health research, not political rhetoric. Second rail: the US embargo is a real factor and must not be denied, but the Special Period's onset is timed to the Soviet collapse (December 1991), not to any 1990s embargo change; the embargo confound is small on this timing. DISTRACTOR MINE: other post-communist adjustments (Poland shock therapy 1990, Russia voucher privatization 1992, East German unification 1990), other caloric-crisis natural experiments (Great Leap 1959-61, North Korea 1993-98).

name: East Germany's Trabant: the calculation debate on wheels
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The DDR's national automobile as a lived demonstration of the calculation problem. T1: from 1957 to 1991 the East German (DDR) state produced the TRABANT ('little satellite'), a two-cycle-engine car with a body of DURAPLAST (a fiberglass-like resin mixed with cotton fibers, because the DDR lacked steel supply chains); the ZWICKAU plant produced approximately 3 million Trabants over 34 years. T2: the DDR set the CAR PRICE below the market-clearing level and used a state-planned waiting list for allocation. Delivery times STRETCHED to 10-15 YEARS for a new Trabant -- families would register a child for a car at birth. T3: the seen-and-unseen chain: SEEN was the price on the sticker, affordable to a worker. UNSEEN was the ten-year queue, the used-Trabant secondary market that priced above the new-car ticket (because you could have it TODAY), and the quality that stagnated for 30 years because Zwickau faced no competitive pressure to redesign the car -- the last Trabants rolled off the line in 1991 with essentially the same 1957 engine. T4: on the day the BERLIN WALL fell (November 9, 1989), and in the weeks after, thousands of East Germans drove Trabants THROUGH the checkpoints into West Berlin; the small blue puffing car became a visual symbol of the DDR's economic condition, and it disappeared from the market almost immediately once West-German used cars became available. T5: Ludwig von MISES's 1920 argument in 'Economic Calculation in the Socialist Commonwealth' predicted this exact pattern: without a price mechanism reflecting real scarcities and consumer preferences, planners cannot know whether to build more Trabants, better Trabants, or a different vehicle entirely -- so they build the same one for 34 years while the world moves on. The Trabant is the calculation debate made physical. Further rungs: the DDR's Wartburg (a slightly larger car) followed the same pattern, with 10-year queues.

CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Trabant' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- 1957-1991 production, Zwickau plant, Duraplast body, two-cycle engine, ~3M produced, 10-15-year waiting lists, price below market-clearing, essentially unchanged 1957 design, November 9 1989 Wall fall images, immediate market disappearance post-unification. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact total production figure; the specific 1957 model designation (Trabant P50 → P60 → P601).

Dinner-test payoff: T2 (families registered a CHILD for a Trabant AT BIRTH) and T4 (the little cars puffing through Checkpoint Charlie the night the Wall fell). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: KNOWLEDGE-PROBLEM (planners cannot know when a design needs updating) + INCENTIVE (no competition means no reason to redesign) + SEEN-VS-UNSEEN (low sticker price vs decade-long queue). Second rail: this ladder does not sneer at the DDR's workers or engineers; the target is the PLANNING SYSTEM that trapped them in a 34-year design freeze. name: Soviet Gosplan and the 200,000-product-category problem
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The concrete numeric reason central planning cannot work. T1: from 1921 to 1991, the Soviet Union planned its whole economy through GOSPLAN (Gosudarstvenniy Planovyy Komitet, the State Planning Committee), headquartered in Moscow. Gosplan set output targets, prices, and interfirm-input allocations for a stated 200,000+ distinct product categories at peak (Gertrude Schroeder + Alec Nove estimates). T2: the calculation-debate reasoning move: for 200,000 products in interlocking supply chains, the number of PAIRWISE PRICES needed to coordinate production is on the order of 200,000 squared / 2 = 20 BILLION price relationships -- and each one changes every day as tastes, weather, harvests, and technology shift. No committee, no supercomputer of any era, can update 20 billion prices in real time. T3: what filled the gap: BLAT (informal favor-trading), TOLKACHI (factory 'pushers' who traveled to Moscow to unstick specific input allocations), STORMING (end-of-plan-period frantic production to meet the quota by nominal weight, sacrificing quality), and the specific joke 'THEY PRETEND TO PAY US AND WE PRETEND TO WORK'. T4: Alec NOVE, a socialist economist and no free-market ideologue, wrote in The Economics of Feasible Socialism (1983) that the calculation problem is REAL and that any large-scale central planning would face it -- his book is one of the most honest inside-the-tradition confrontations with the Mises-Hayek argument. T5: the punchline is empirical: on December 26, 1991, the Soviet Union voted itself out of existence, Gosplan closed, and the 20-billion-price coordination problem was handed back to a market with no committee needed. Mises's 1920 prediction that socialist calculation cannot rationally allocate resources was vindicated by the sequence 1920 argument -> 1991 collapse -> post-1992 empirical evidence that market economies coordinated the same product categories without any committee, and better. Further rungs: Vasili Nalimov's 1971 information-theory paper on Soviet planning attempted to formalize the impossibility.
source: PRIMARY: Alec Nove, The Economics of Feasible Socialism (1983); Gertrude Schroeder, 'The Soviet Economy on a Treadmill of Reforms' (Joint Economic Committee, US Congress, 1979); Vasili Nalimov, 'Reality of the Unreal' (1971). CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Gosplan' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- 1921-1991 duration, 200,000-product-category peak estimate (Schroeder + Nove), blat / tolkachi / storming as documented workarounds, the December 26 1991 dissolution date. Mises, Economic Calculation in the Socialist Commonwealth (1920, Mises Institute translation); Hayek, ed., Collectivist Economic Planning (1935). CORROBORATE AT BUILD: the 200,000-product-category figure (Schroeder's Joint Economic Committee report is the standard cite); Nalimov's exact 1971 information-theory argument.
framing_note: The RIGOROUS calculation-debate ladder, keyed to a specific quantitative reason the planning problem is impossible in principle rather than merely difficult in practice. Dinner-test payoff: T2 (20 BILLION pairwise prices need updating every day for a large economy) and T3 (workers said 'they pretend to pay us and we pretend to work'). REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: KNOWLEDGE-PROBLEM in its cleanest form (Mises + Hayek + Nove) + specific quantitative version. ACCURACY RAIL: the 200,000-product-category figure is Gertrude Schroeder's peak estimate; the 20-billion pairwise-price number is derived from that and is a heuristic teaching device, not a Gosplan-cited figure; label it as such. Second rail: Alec Nove was a SOCIALIST -- his acknowledgment of the calculation problem's reality is powerful precisely because he was inside the tradition trying to salvage it; do NOT recast him as an Austrian. ANTI-RESTATEMENT: stem describes Gosplan, the product-category count, the workaround culture; the answer is the REASONING MOVE (Mises calculation problem) or the SPECIFIC WORKAROUND (blat, tolkachi, storming) or Nove's inside-the-tradition confirmation. history_overlap: HISTORY owns the USSR as a political state and the December 1991 dissolution; economics owns the calculation-problem analysis of why Gosplan could not work.

name: North Korea's Public Distribution System collapse: the Arduous March
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The famine that isolated the mechanism of central-distribution collapse. T1: from 1957 to the early 1990s the North Korean state fed its people through the PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM (PDS) -- state-run ration shops distributed grain, oil, and other necessities according to job classification and political loyalty. Private markets were essentially banned. T2: when Soviet aid collapsed in 1991 and Chinese aid contracted mid-decade, the PDS began to break down; by 1994-95 many regions received rations at a fraction of the stated amount. In 1995 severe floods struck the country; the famine that Koreans call the ARDUOUS MARCH (KOJEIN HAENGGUN, 1993-1998) had begun. T3: Marcus NOLAND + Stephan HAGGARD's careful 2007 study 'Famine in North Korea' estimated 600,000 to 2.5 million deaths during the Arduous March -- an enormous range because the regime published no data. What both scholars agree on: the collapse was PRODUCED by the failure of the PDS itself; regions cut off from Pyongyang's distribution centrally suffered worst. T4: what saved millions was the emergence of illegal MARKETS -- the JANGMADANG ('market grounds'), initially bicycle-basket traders selling food across regions in defiance of the ban. Yeonmi PARK and Hyeonseo LEE, both defectors, describe in their memoirs how their mothers and grandmothers walked hours to jangmadang markets to feed their families with rice bought outside the PDS. By 2019 defector-survey estimates suggested that ~70-80% of North Korean private consumption flowed through jangmadang markets, formally illegal but tolerated because the alternative was renewed famine. T5: the reasoning-move payoff: North Korea 1993-98 is the sharpest modern demonstration that central-distribution failure is a FAMINE MECHANISM in itself -- Mises 1920's argument in its most literal form. The recovery came not from better central planning but from the SPONTANEOUS EMERGENCE of markets in defiance of the law -- Hayek's spontaneous order operating in the world's most totalitarian environment. Further rungs: Andrei Lankov's 'North of the DMZ' documents the jangmadang's development in detail.
source: PRIMARY: Marcus Noland + Stephan Haggard, Famine in North Korea (Columbia UP 2007); Andrei Lankov, North of the DMZ (McFarland 2007); Yeonmi Park, In Order to Live (2015); Hyeonseo Lee, The Girl with Seven Names (2015). CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'North Korean famine' and 'Jangmadang' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- 1993-98 famine, PDS collapse origin, 600K-2.5M death range, jangmadang emergence, ~70-80% consumption share via markets by 2019, Yeonmi Park / Hyeonseo Lee memoirs. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: the Noland-Haggard specific death-range estimate; the current-year jangmadang consumption share (defector surveys give a range).

ACCURACY RAIL: the 600K-2.5M death range is honest -- the regime released no data. name: China's Household Responsibility System 1978-83
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The state's own empirical vindication of the calculation debate. T1: after the Great Leap Forward (1958-62) and Cultural Revolution (1966-76), Chinese agriculture in 1978 was organized in PEOPLE'S COMMUNES (renmin gongshe) -- large collective farms where output belonged to the commune and was distributed by work-points assigned by cadres. Grain output had stagnated for a decade. T2: in November 1978, farmers in XIAOGANG VILLAGE (Anhui Province) secretly signed a 'life-and-death contract' in which each family took responsibility for a specific plot and agreed to deliver a set quota to the state, keeping any surplus for themselves. They signed knowing that if discovered they could be executed. T3: Xiaogang's grain output ROSE about 6x in one year; the practice spread; by 1983 the HOUSEHOLD RESPONSIBILITY SYSTEM (jiating lianchan chengbao zeren zhi) was legalized nationwide under Deng Xiaoping. T4: economist Justin Yifu LIN in his 1992 China Economic Review paper 'Rural Reforms and Agricultural Growth in China' quantified the effect: Chinese grain output rose approximately 33% between 1978 and 1984, and Lin's decomposition attributed roughly HALF of the productivity gain to the incentive-restoration of the Household Responsibility System (not to fertilizer, weather, or better seed). T5: the reasoning-move payoff: this is the STATE'S OWN EMPIRICAL VINDICATION of the calculation and incentive arguments. The identical land, the identical farmers, the identical seed, weather, and technology, produced dramatically more grain when the RESIDUAL CLAIM (the right to keep surplus) was restored to the family. Mises 1920's incentive argument and Hayek 1945's knowledge argument were both vindicated by China's own reform, in one country, over five years. Deng's phrase 'it does not matter whether the cat is black or white as long as it catches mice' is the meta-lesson. Further rungs: Xiaogang village's contract is preserved in the Beijing museum of modern Chinese history.

name: India's License Raj 1947-1991
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The world's most elaborate industrial-licensing system and what its 1991 collapse revealed. T1: from independence in 1947 to 1991, India ran its economy on Nehru-era Fabian-socialist principles that came to be called the LICENSE RAJ ('rule by permits'). Any Indian firm wishing to open a factory, expand capacity, import a machine, hire above a certain scale, produce a new product, or set prices, needed government LICENSES -- often 80+ separate approvals from central and state ministries. T2: the seen-and-unseen: SEEN was the stability, planning-rationality, and 'self-reliance' rhetoric. UNSEEN was the growth Indians did NOT experience -- India's GDP per capita grew ~1% per year 1950-1980 (the sardonic 'HINDU RATE OF GROWTH' term coined by economist Raj Krishna), while South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, and Hong Kong grew 5-8x faster over the same decades, starting from the same postwar baseline. T3: the specific mechanism Anne KRUEGER identified in her 1974 American Economic Review paper 'The Political Economy of the Rent-Seeking Society' drew directly on Indian license-raj empirical work: because a license was worth more than the underlying resource (an import license alone captured a huge deadweight above competitive market prices), firms spent vast resources LOBBYING for licenses rather than producing goods -- classic RENT-SEEKING behavior. Krueger estimated rent-seeking dissipation at up to 7% of Indian GDP. T4: on JULY 24, 1991, facing a balance-of-payments crisis, Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha RAO and Finance Minister Manmohan SINGH delivered a budget that dismantled the license raj -- ending most industrial-licensing requirements, cutting tariffs, permitting foreign direct investment. T5: the empirical result: India's growth rate approximately DOUBLED, then accelerated further; hundreds of millions rose out of extreme poverty over the following three decades; per-capita income more than QUADRUPLED in real terms 1991-2020. Arvind Panagariya's 'India: The Emerging Giant' (2008) documents the reform-to-growth chain in detail. The reasoning move: government-licensing that reduces the profitability of production reduces production; removing the licenses restores it. Further rungs: Bibek Debroy + Amit Kapoor's recent surveys extend the analysis to state-level variation.

CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'License Raj' and 'Economic liberalisation in India' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- 1947-1991 duration, 80+ approvals typical, 'Hindu rate of growth' term origin (Raj Krishna), July 24 1991 Manmohan Singh budget, Narasimha Rao PM, Krueger's 7% GDP rent-dissipation estimate, post-1991 growth doubling. Dinner-test payoff: T2 (India's growth per capita was ~1% per year for 30 years while its neighbors grew 5x faster from the same start) and T5 (per-capita income QUADRUPLED in real terms after the 1991 reforms). name: COVID-era PPE price gouging and the Munger water example
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The reasoning move applied to a case every child watched happen. T1: during the early weeks of the COVID-19 pandemic (March-April 2020), most US states enforced ANTI-PRICE-GOUGING laws that made it illegal to sell N95 masks, hand sanitizer, and toilet paper above the pre-emergency price -- and enforcement agencies threatened fines and jail. T2: the seen-and-unseen: SEEN was the ceiling that felt fair. UNSEEN was the SHORTAGE -- masks were UNAVAILABLE at any legal price in most stores for weeks; hand sanitizer disappeared; toilet paper was rationed; entrepreneurs who wanted to import PPE or manufacture new supply had no signal that the higher price would clear costs. T3: the Michael MUNGER example (Duke economist, widely-cited): in September 2004, after Hurricane Frances hit Florida, a Kentucky entrepreneur named John Shepperson rented a U-Haul, bought 19 generators, drove them 600 miles to a Florida county without power, and offered them at approximately double what he paid. Florida police ARRESTED him under the state's anti-price-gouging law; the generators were CONFISCATED. Munger's point: Shepperson's family did without power, the Florida county did without generators, and no other Kentucky entrepreneur will take the same risk next hurricane. The reasoning move: an anti-gouging law removes the SIGNAL that would attract emergency supply. T4: Steven Horwitz + others documented the identical pattern in 2020 COVID PPE. The clearest natural experiment came when some states did NOT enforce gouging laws on PPE (Tennessee briefly waived enforcement); those markets restocked measurably faster. T5: the reasoning-move payoff: Munger frames it as 'PRICE GOUGING IS THE SOLUTION, NOT THE PROBLEM' -- the high price is the market's shout to producers and importers 'HERE, RUSH SUPPLY HERE'; the anti-gouging law silences the shout and prolongs the shortage. This is Bastiat's seen-vs-unseen applied to any emergency: the SEEN is the fair-feeling ceiling; the UNSEEN is every entrepreneur who does not drive a U-Haul of generators or a container of N95s because the reward has been criminalized. Further rungs: Sowell's Basic Economics quotes the Shepperson case explicitly.

(Library of Economics and Liberty, January 8 2007); Steven Horwitz + others in 2020 pandemic-response essays (Mercatus Center, AIER); news coverage of John Shepperson case (2004 Kentucky Post and Florida sources). CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Price gouging' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- Shepperson case 2004 Hurricane Frances, US state anti-gouging law patterns, COVID-era enforcement, Munger's framing. Sowell, Basic Economics 5th ed., ch. 3. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: Munger's exact essay title and date; Shepperson case specifics (some sources spell it Sheperson).

name: FDR's Agricultural Adjustment Act 1933 and the six million pigs
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The New Deal case study Bastiat would scream at. T1: in MAY 1933, in the depths of the Great Depression, President Franklin ROOSEVELT signed the AGRICULTURAL ADJUSTMENT ACT (AAA) -- a law designed to RAISE farm prices by REDUCING agricultural output. The law paid farmers to plow up crops already planted, kill livestock, and leave acreage idle. T2: the most famous case: in the fall of 1933, under the AAA's emergency hog program, approximately 6 MILLION PIGS were slaughtered -- many purchased from farmers by the government specifically to destroy them. Millions of pounds of pork were rendered into fertilizer or dumped rather than shipped to the tens of millions of unemployed Americans standing in BREADLINES in the same cities. T3: the seen-and-unseen: SEEN was the higher price for the surviving hogs, which was the intended effect for the farmer's cash flow. UNSEEN was the FOOD -- rendering pork into fertilizer while children in Chicago were hungry made the AAA a national embarrassment; Henry Wallace, Roosevelt's Secretary of Agriculture, was booed and had to publicly explain the policy on the radio. T4: the reasoning move: this is BASTIAT'S BROKEN WINDOW applied to a whole industry. The AAA's advocates focused on the seen benefit to farm cash-flow; they ignored the unseen destruction of food and the incentive-distortion that would make farmers PLANT LESS deliberately in future seasons. Milton Friedman + Anna Schwartz later argued in A Monetary History that the New Deal's supply-restriction programs (AAA plus the National Recovery Administration's price supports) PROLONGED the Great Depression by artificially raising costs and prices during a period of monetary contraction. T5: the Supreme Court struck down the original AAA in JANUARY 1936 (United States v. Butler) as an unconstitutional use of the taxing power; Congress passed a modified version in 1938 that survived and still forms the skeleton of US farm-subsidy programs today. The reasoning move: government-directed destruction of production to raise prices concentrates benefits on the producers and disperses costs (higher prices, less food, tax burden) on everyone else -- Mancur Olson's dispersed-cost / concentrated-benefit dynamic in its founding case. Further rungs: Amity Shlaes's The Forgotten Man (2007) treats the AAA in detail as one of the New Deal's economic-damage centers.

CONSULTED: Grokipedia 'Agricultural Adjustment Act' (browser, 2026-09-05) -- May 1933 signature, ~6M hog slaughter, Henry Wallace controversy, breadline juxtaposition, United States v. Butler 1936 strike-down, 1938 successor act. CORROBORATE AT BUILD: exact hog-slaughter figure (5-6M range in sources); Wallace's specific public statements defending the policy.

REASONING-MOVE HIERARCHY: SEEN-VS-UNSEEN (higher farm price vs destroyed food) + DISPERSED-COSTS / CONCENTRATED-BENEFITS (Olson's founding case) + Friedman's monetary-contraction critique. ACCURACY RAIL: the ~6M pigs figure is the standard estimate; some sources say ~5M, some ~6.2M; state as 'approximately 6 million'. Second rail: do NOT sneer at FDR or the desperation of 1933; the case study is the MECHANISM; the AAA's designers believed they were helping farmers, and the mechanism nevertheless destroyed food while people were hungry. name: US milk supports and 'government cheese'
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The dairy program that made mountains of cheese while telling everyone milk was scarce. T1: since the Agricultural Act of 1949, the US government has maintained a MILK PRICE SUPPORT program -- promising to purchase all the surplus milk, butter, and cheese American dairy farmers produce at above-market prices, then store or dispose of the surplus. T2: throughout the 1970s and 1980s the program worked exactly as economic theory predicted: the guaranteed above-market price led farmers to produce MORE milk than consumers wanted at that price; the government dutifully bought and stored the surplus, primarily as processed cheese in refrigerated warehouses. T3: by 1981 the US government owned OVER 500 MILLION POUNDS of surplus cheese sitting in caves and warehouses across the country. This became a national embarrassment; the Reagan administration announced a distribution program to give the cheese away, and 'GOVERNMENT CHEESE' entered American vocabulary as a name for the specific processed cheese loaves handed out through food banks and welfare programs. T4: economist Milton FRIEDMAN in Free to Choose treats the dairy support as a textbook DISPERSED-COSTS-CONCENTRATED-BENEFITS case -- roughly 100,000 dairy farm households benefit; 330 million Americans pay higher prices and taxes for the program's continuation, but each individual American's cost is small enough that no one campaigns against it, while the dairy lobby campaigns hard for it. Mancur Olson's Logic of Collective Action (1965) predicted exactly this asymmetry. T5: the reasoning move: a permanent above-market price signal produces PERMANENT surplus, which produces PERMANENT government purchase and storage, at PERMANENT public cost. The program has persisted for 75+ years despite continuous economist critique across the political spectrum -- a Sowell 'compared to what?' moment: compared to a market that clears at the market-clearing price with occasional bad years for farmers, the dairy support system has been extraordinarily expensive for extraordinarily modest benefit to a small concentrated constituency. Further rungs: the program was reformed in 2014 (Dairy Margin Coverage) but the underlying above-market-support structure persists.

name: The ethanol mandate and the 2007 Guatemalan tortilla riots
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The US corn mandate that hit the world's poorest with a food-price shock. T1: the Energy Policy Act of 2005 established the RENEWABLE FUEL STANDARD (RFS); the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 EXPANDED it to require ~15 billion gallons of ethanol in the US gasoline supply by 2015. To meet the mandate, US corn-ethanol production surged; by 2011, approximately 40% of the US corn crop was being diverted from food to fuel. T2: the seen-and-unseen: SEEN was the domestic-energy-independence rhetoric and the direct benefit to Iowa + Illinois + Nebraska corn farmers and to ethanol-blender interests (ADM, POET). UNSEEN was the world CORN PRICE, which roughly DOUBLED between 2006 and 2013, and the world food-price index generally, which rose steeply and hit importing countries hardest. T3: in JANUARY 2007, MEXICO experienced the TORTILLA RIOTS -- tens of thousands protested in Mexico City as the price of maize tortillas (a staple food) had roughly doubled in months, tracking the US corn-price spike. Similar food-price protests broke out in Egypt, Haiti, and elsewhere through 2007-2008; the World Bank estimated food-price rises pushed 100+ million people back into extreme poverty. T4: the reasoning move: an ARTIFICIAL DEMAND SHOCK created by government mandate (US corn diverted to fuel) transmits through global commodity markets to the food of the world's poorest. This is Bastiat's seen-vs-unseen at PLANETARY SCALE: the seen is the US energy-independence talking point; the unseen is the Guatemalan family whose tortilla now costs twice as much because of a US law. Nobel-laureate agricultural economist C. Peter Timmer, biofuel researchers Sudhir Chella Rajan + others, and the World Bank's Donald Mitchell (2008 internal memo, later leaked) all documented the US-ethanol-to-world-food-price link. T5: the RFS has been repeatedly extended and modestly reformed but remains the largest US biofuel program; the reasoning-move applies to any mandate that creates artificial demand for a food crop. Further rungs: the corn-ethanol mandate is separately criticized on ENERGY-BALANCE grounds (Cornell's David Pimentel argued net energy from corn ethanol is close to zero or negative once fertilizer and processing energy are counted).

name: Zimbabwe's June 26 2007 price-halving order
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The fastest empty-shelf demonstration in modern history. T1: on JUNE 26, 2007, Zimbabwean president Robert MUGABE, facing rising prices caused primarily by the government's own money-printing to finance the budget, ORDERED all retail prices in Zimbabwe cut roughly IN HALF, with penalties including imprisonment for retailers who did not comply. Police and army units enforced the order in supermarkets in Harare and Bulawayo. T2: within 48 HOURS, the seen-and-unseen played out at time-lapse speed: SEEN was the low mandated price on the label; UNSEEN was the merchandise itself -- shelves were EMPTIED, largely by consumers rushing to buy at below-cost prices (Mugabe supporters framed this as 'people finally getting what they need'), but most goods vanished into black markets or private hoarding. T3: within days, FACTORIES shut down -- meat processors, dairies, bakeries -- because there was no way to produce a loaf of bread at a mandated price that was less than the cost of the flour, yeast, and fuel to bake it. The Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries reported that hundreds of manufacturers closed operations or laid off staff within the first two weeks of the order. T4: WITHIN THREE MONTHS the order was quietly abandoned as unenforceable; empty shelves and factory closures had produced a catastrophic economic collapse on top of the already-severe hyperinflation. Zimbabwe went on to print the famous 100-TRILLION-DOLLAR NOTE in January 2009 as the currency collapsed entirely, and formally adopted the US dollar in 2009. T5: the reasoning-move payoff: this is the fastest, cleanest, most compressed real-time demonstration of price-control-mechanism-to-empty-shelves in modern economic history. From order to visible collapse: 48 hours. Every prediction Mises 1920 made about socialist calculation, and Hayek 1945 made about knowledge and prices, unfolded on Zimbabwe's supermarket shelves in less time than it takes to run a school semester. Further rungs: journalist Robert Guest's 'The Shackled Continent' (2004) documented the run-up; economist Steve Hanke's contemporaneous Cato Institute writing tracked the collapse in real time.

name: Poland's Balcerowicz Plan 1990: shock therapy that worked
strand: Price controls + modern socialism case studies
scope: The post-communist reform sequence Poland ran and Russia botched. T1: after the June 1989 Solidarity election victory, the new Polish government appointed the economist Leszek BALCEROWICZ (a Warsaw School of Economics professor) as finance minister; he assembled a package of ten laws, passed by parliament in late 1989 and effective JANUARY 1, 1990, that came to be called the BALCEROWICZ PLAN or 'shock therapy'. T2: the plan's core moves were: (a) IMMEDIATE LIBERALIZATION of prices on almost all goods (ending Communist-era price controls overnight); (b) currency CONVERTIBILITY of the zloty; (c) hard-budget constraints on state enterprises (no more soft bailouts); (d) opening to foreign trade; (e) beginning of privatization of state enterprises. T3: the first year was PAINFUL -- GDP contracted about 12% in 1990 and again in 1991; unemployment rose from near-zero (nominal Communist full employment) to over 12%; inflation initially spiked. Balcerowicz and the government took huge political heat. T4: from 1992 onwards Polish GDP grew CONTINUOUSLY -- not a single year of contraction between 1992 and the 2008 crisis (a stretch matched by essentially no other European economy). By 2019, Poland's real GDP per capita had approximately TRIPLED from its 1990 low; Warsaw became a modern European capital; the country accessed the EU in 2004 and remained one of the fastest-growing member economies. T5: the reasoning-move payoff: the Balcerowicz Plan is the cleanest post-1989 test of whether the calculation-debate reforms should be done FAST or GRADUAL. Poland went fast; Russia's Yeltsin-era voucher-privatization process 1992-95 went gradual (in some respects), was captured by insiders, and produced the oligarch collapse of the 1990s. The comparison teaches that HALF-MEASURES (nominal price liberalization without hard budget constraints and without institutional protection) fail; a coherent package with hard-budget discipline enables the Mises-Hayek market mechanism to actually work. Further rungs: Jeffrey Sachs (Harvard) advised the Polish reform team and is a co-associated name with 'shock therapy'.
